pr_template.content:
Read the [Definition of Ready for Review](https://ultimaker.atlassian.net/l/cp/U0ErL5NA) for more details on the rationale behind this PR template

## Description
_A concise explanation of the changes made in this Pull Request. Consider adding_ \
_- Why this change was necessary_ \
_- Notable decisions made_ \
_- Out of scope items_ \
_- Screenshots/GIFs for visual changes_

## How has this been tested
_A brief description of what was tested, how, and on what machines. \
If tests remain to be done, also mention that here!_


## Ready for Review Checklist
To help with deciding if this PR is RFR, use this checklist.

The author confirms that:
- [ ] the author has **self-reviewed** this work and is highly confident about the quality
- [ ] this work satisfies all **acceptance criteria** that are stated in the linked ticket
- [ ] this work has been **tested** on all product families and the process and results are documented in the above section
- [ ] The **description** above is concise yet complete
- [ ] the reviewer has been offered a **walkthrough** (if needed)
- [ ] the code is **cleaned** from any rubbish (e.g. meaningless comments, log-spamming, etc...)
- [ ] remaining `#TODO` **comments** mention a Jira ticket number
- [ ] all **CI** checks are passing
- [ ] all **commits** are (re)structured to be meaningful and clearly arranged, and all are prepended with the ticket number for traceability

observations.title: The repository documents its own architecture in-tree
observations.question: Read these before writing anything about this repository's architecture. Which of them state a convention that is a correctness requirement rather than a style preference, and which name a footgun a newcomer would hit? Anything already written here belongs in AGENTS.md as a CITATION, never as a paraphrase that will drift from the original.
observations.draft_rule: Before changing `<area>`, read `<doc path>` — it is the authored convention for this subsystem. State the constraint it carries (`<constraint>`) and cite the document rather than restating it here.

observations.title: This repository is a provider or consumer in a submodule graph
observations.question: For each submodule: does this repository merely consume it, or does it own it? Who else pins the same submodule, and what is the ordering discipline when a change spans both trees (innermost first, push the submodule branch before moving the parent pointer)?
observations.draft_rule: Submodule pointers in this repository are moved only after the corresponding change is merged and pushed in `<submodule repo>`. Never commit inside a submodule tree from this checkout. A pointer bump is its own commit and names the upstream revision it moves to.

observations.title: Commits are small and tightly scoped
observations.question: Should the scope rule name a concrete file-count expectation derived from this repository's own history?
observations.draft_rule: Keep commits tightly scoped: this repository's median commit touches 1 files. A commit touching more than 5 files needs an explicit justification in the message.

observations.title: History keeps merge commits
evidence: 80/300 sampled commits are merges (mostly pull request merges)
observations.question: Is the merge commit intentional (preserving branch topology), and should agents therefore NOT rebase published branches?
observations.draft_rule: This repository preserves merge topology. Do not rewrite or rebase branches that have already been pushed; integrate with merges.

observations.title: Releases are tagged with v-prefixed semantic versions
observations.question: Do version bumps have a required home (packaging metadata, recipe file, CMake project version) that must move together with the tag?
observations.draft_rule: Release tags follow v-prefixed semantic versions. When bumping a version, update every location that carries it (<list them>) in the same commit.
